Engineering estimate · v1.2

Operating parameters

Default feed moisture is 49.13% ARB and raw-coal ash is 3.38% ARB from the original SAK analysis associated with the PT trial series (Excel, All (Value Only), row 3); PT5 is the default trial. The PT1 reference normalization is a model assumption needed to reconcile PT trial wet-feed results with a separate dryer. Measured PT wet-char moisture is displayed as a quality diagnostic, not added to the plant water balance after drying.

Calibration warning. The 60–70 minute AC recovery and iodine results were obtained with 650°C carbonization, not PT1–PT6. Estimated product rates and gas heating values are not guaranteed pilot-plant results.

Ash mass balance: Ash retained in final AC = raw coal feed (kg/day) × raw coal ash (ARB mass fraction). Final AC ash (wt%) = retained ash / final activated carbon × 100. Raw ash is conserved through drying, pyrolysis, and activation; no ash exits in dust, gas, or washing. PT char ash assays remain reference diagnostics; varying raw ash changes modeled char ash and the available organic fixed-carbon inventory.

Mass basis · kg output / kg feed

Steam-derived H₂ increases gas mass, so combustible-gas output can exceed its share of coal mass; the percentages are yields relative to raw coal, not fractions that must sum to 100%. Gas includes pyrolysis gas and characterized H₂/CO/CO₂, but excludes uncharacterized activation volatiles and furnace flue gas.

Dry combustible process gas composition & quality

Dry mole/volume %. CO₂ and inert components are not combustible. Pyrolysis gas uses a provisional P4-inspired composition; activation gas uses reaction stoichiometry and adjustable water-gas shift.

Source basis, assumptions and exclusions

Measured: PT1–PT6 char yields, moisture, ash, volatile matter, fixed carbon, elemental carbon and pyrolysis oil/gas yields in Data Trial Pyrolysis Batu Bara (20250203).xlsx. Only P4-240927 is used as the P4 report reference. Test 1: 73 g AC/500 g raw coal, iodine 752.19 mg/g, 950°C × 60 min. Test 2: 60 g/500 g, iodine 781.47 mg/g, 950°C × 70 min.

Modeled: A 200°C dryer removes the input moisture. Because direct wet-feed PT1–PT3 dry-char yields exceed the dry solids available in the new raw coal, the simulator normalizes PT1 to an assumed maximum dry-char recovery (90% by default) and scales the other trials according to relative measured dry-char yield. Dry-pyrolysis residual mass is split between reaction water (10% of nonchar dry-coal material), oil and gas (oil/gas ratio follows each PT trial). These allocations are engineering assumptions, not source measurements.

Activation: Test 1 and 2 whole-feed AC recoveries are scaled with relative measured fixed-carbon inventory compared with PT5. Ash stays in solid AC. The remainder of the fixed-carbon inventory above final AC carbon is treated as steam-reactive carbon, capped by available steam. Measured wet-char moisture is a diagnostic of the original PT tests, not a separately added moisture stream after complete upstream drying. Fixed carbon is only a proxy for reactive carbon. Residual volatile/inert material leaving the activation vessel is accounted as uncharacterized vapor, and is not assigned an invented combustible heating value. The reaction model includes C + H₂O → CO + H₂ and a user-set CO + H₂O → CO₂ + H₂ shift fraction.

Heating value: calculated from modeled dry H₂, CO and CH₄ using LHV values of approximately 10.78, 12.63 and 35.8 MJ/Nm³. Pyrolysis gas composition is a proxy (H₂ 47.45%, CO 19.49%, CH₄ 11.34%, CO₂ 6%, inert other 15.72% by volume). The last two fractions are assumptions, not direct trial measurements. Actual syngas quality requires GC analysis.

Not included as saleable process gas: furnace combustion exhaust, unreacted wet steam, dryer offgas, and unidentified volatile gas/vapors. Fuel combustion and heat-recovery boiler are not closed in this version; furnace flue gas cannot be calculated credibly without burner fuel split, combustion air and excess oxygen. The five main physical streams are AC, oil, water, process gas, and separate combustion exhaust.

Process System Diagram

Integrated drying at 200°C, pyrolysis at 400–500°C, steam activation at 950°C, condensation, fuel recycling, waste-heat steam production and furnace exhaust treatment.
